author: New China TV
description:
Hongshan Culture is one of China's most important prehistoric archaeological cultures dating back approximately 5,000 to 6,000 years. It had a profound impact on the subsequent development of Chinese civilization.
The Niuheliang site, discovered in 1981 in the city of Chaoyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, represents a milestone in the study of Hongshan. It's renowned for the wealth of exquisite jade artifacts, statues, altars and stone tombs discovered there.
The 2026 Conference on Hongshan Culture recently concluded in Chaoyang, bringing together scholars and diplomats from around the world. What fascinates them most about Hongshan? And how can this ancient heritage inspire dialogue and mutual learning across millennia and continents? We asked them. Here's what they told us.
title: What makes Hongshan Culture fascinating? Global voices from Chaoyang

author: New China TV
description:
Hefei in east China's Anhui Province has held a series of themed markets which took advantage of local cultural and tourism resources to boost consumption.
At Huiyuan Garden scenic area, a cultural market featuring creative products, folk songs and performances, fish-shaped lantern parades and local delicacies offers visitors an immersive experience of Anhui culture.
In Dawei Town, a grape-themed market provides a platform for local farmers to promote agricultural products. Visitors can taste various varieties of grapes and grape-based drinks, purchase agricultural products with discounts, and participate in study tours.
By integrating cultural experiences, leisure activities and consumption, these themed markets have succeeded in attracting visitors while creating new opportunities for local tourism and rural industries. xhtxs.cn/bd7U
title: GLOBALink | Hefei embraces new tourism trends with various themed markets
